# Service Participation Depth in Experiential Services: Media Touchpoints and Supportive Practices {.citation_title}

<p class="citation_author">Hikaru Goto</p>

<p class="citation"><em>Journal of Services Marketing</em>, 1–11 (2026). DOI: <a href="https://doi.org/10.1108/JSM-05-2026-0444">10.1108/JSM-05-2026-0444</a></p>

<p class="publication-meta">Accepted: 17 October 2026 · Published online: 10 November 2026</p>

## Abstract

**Purpose.** This study examines how media touchpoints, involvement and supportive practices are associated with any live attendance and attendance intensity in spectator sport services.

**Design/methodology/approach.** Individual-level data from the Sports Life Survey 2024 (Adults) were analyzed using a two-part Bayesian sparse model: a Bernoulli-logit model for any attendance and a zero-truncated negative binomial model for conditional attendance intensity. Prior predictive checks and sensitivity analyses assessed key modeling decisions.

**Findings.** Any attendance showed positive posterior associations with online J.League viewing, televised Nippon Professional Baseball viewing, transportation support, televised J.League viewing and sport-club involvement. Online Nippon Professional Baseball viewing remained positive across specifications, but its main-model 95% credible interval narrowly included zero. Conditional attendance intensity was positively associated with online J.League viewing and preparation support. Sample-averaged predictions indicated a 22.9-percentage-point difference in any-attendance probability and a 2.71-attendance difference in the conditional expected count for online J.League viewing; preparation support showed a 2.79-attendance difference in the conditional expected count.

**Practical implications.** Managers should distinguish initiatives aimed at generating physical participation from those aimed at increasing intensity among attendees and should test media-linked attendance communications and coordination-support tools separately.

**Originality.** The study decomposes service participation into occurrence and conditional intensity and jointly examines mediated touchpoints, involvement and supportive practices within a high-dimensional Bayesian framework.
